title: A cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 8–9)
hook: the Macedonians gave out of poverty; God loves a cheerful giver
tomorrow: what do you say when someone claims you got it all secondhand?

segments.voice: Yesterday's word: reconciliation, and the line all things new. Today Paul turns to money, and somehow it's about joy.

A fundraiser link drops in the group chat, and the first person to chip in is the one who just lost shifts at work. It happens. Paul saw it happen. The churches of Macedonia, he tells Corinth, were in "a great trial of affliction" and "deep poverty," and they gave anyway, to a collection for poor believers far away. More than they could afford, he says, and nobody had to ask them twice. How?
screen: `THE FIRST ONE TO CHIP IN.` → `DEEP POVERTY, AND THEY GAVE.` → `HOW?`

segments.voice: Paul's answer is joy: "the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality." Joy plus poverty added up to generosity. They "first gave their own selves to the Lord," and the money followed. And he won't set a price: "If there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not." Then the heart of it: "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver." Now a neighbor. Muslims keep sayings of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in the hadith collections. One says that your smile in your brother's face is charity. Another says every kind act is charity. Shared ground: a gift is weighed by the heart, not the size, and even a face can give. The honest difference: Islam also has zakat, a required giving that is one of the pillars of the faith, alongside the free giving called sadaqa. Paul's collection is free will, "not of necessity," though some Christians keep a set tithe. Two houses, both glad about giving, each with its own shape for it.
screen: `JOY PLUS POVERTY = LIBERALITY.` · `BY WHAT YOU HAVE, NOT WHAT YOU DON'T.` · `A SMILE IS CHARITY: THE HADITH.` · `ZAKAT REQUIRED; PAUL'S GIFT FREE.` · then, large: `A CHEERFUL GIVER.`

segments.voice: Let your face soften into a small smile, even alone in the room, and notice what it does to your shoulders and your breath. Bring to mind one person you'll see today, and one small thing you could give them: time, a hand, a greeting. Keep the smile while you picture handing it over.
A cheerful giver. Paul's picture of giving from a willing heart, by what you have, not grudgingly.
The line to keep: a cheerful giver, glad to give by what you have, however small. See you soon.

chat.meaning: Paul says give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly, for God loves a cheerful giver. A hadith calls a smile charity. Shared ground, each in its own words.

notes: Wisdom day, unity thread: shared ground with Islam, in its own sources (paraphrased hadith: a smile for your brother is charity, Tirmidhi 1956; every kind act is charity, Bukhari 6021 / Muslim 1005), and one honest difference: zakat is required giving and a pillar (Bukhari 8), alongside voluntary sadaqa, while Paul's collection is 'not of necessity' (9:7), with 'some Christians' keeping a set tithe. Nothing is ranked or called 'the same'. A Muslim reader should confirm the hadith paraphrases, numbering and the zakat/sadaqa description; a Christian Keeper the tithe line.
'The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him' follows the Islam path's first-mention convention.
'More than they could afford, and nobody had to ask them twice' paraphrases 8:3–4 ('beyond their power they were willing of themselves; praying us with much intreaty'); confirm.
The collection's destination: 'poor believers far away' (the KJV says 'the saints'; Romans 15:26 names the poor saints at Jerusalem). No claim beyond that.
howItsDone names offerings, tithes and alms side by side without ranking; confirm that some churches read 9:7 at the offering.
